messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: [PAGER] smart-routing.alert — elevated 5xx and latency spikes across eu-west regions. Auto-fallback to other regions observed. Pager: paged eng-sre. Incident link: https://pager.example/INC-4312

alex: seeing lots of downstream 502s from the model service after fallback kicks in. Traces show requests that should stay in eu-west-1 are being routed to us-east-1 and hitting variant 'gptx-small' which rejects some newer ops.

maria: confirmed - errors begin ~14:02 UTC, spike lasted ~10m then oscillated. Some requests succeed but with +600ms added. Could be stale DNS at edge causing inconsistent region resolution.

lee: I'm oncall, looking at smart-routing logs now. 

samir: quick check — smart-routing policy rollout v2.3.7 was promoted at 13:45 UTC. It introduced a new fallback precedence that accidentally listed 'variant: gptx-small' ahead of regional parity variants. Suspect mis-order + stale DNS = loop where fallback triggers, then DNS resolves back -> oscillation.

priya: DNS check: partial propagation on eu-edge RRSet. Some PoPs still resolving the old IP set that points to global loadbalancer which then forwards to us-east. Dig outputs:```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
eu-edge.example.  60 IN A  3.4.5.6
# but some resolvers still return 52.11.22.33 (us-east VIP)
```

alex: copying smart-routing policy snippet (current active):
```
fallback_order:
  - region: us-east-1  # introduced by mistake
  - region: eu-west-1
  - variant: gptx-small
  - variant: gptx-large
```
This ordering is wrong — policy should prefer same-region variants first and fall back to compatible variant families, not a different region's VIP.

maria: customer impact? CS ops — any incoming tickets?

cs_ops: we have 8 inbound support threads, 2 high-priority customers reporting elevated latencies and intermittent 502s on hosted API. Status page updated to "degraded". Notified account leads for affected customers.

lee: mitigation plan: 1) pause routing policy rollout (rollback to v2.3.6) 2) add a temporary override to prefer same-region targets 3) ask DNS to force immediate rrset refresh / lower TTL 4) flush edge caches where possible. I'll kick off 1 and 2 now.

samir: how to pause? CLI command:
```
redwood routing rollout pause --policy smart-routing --id v2.3.7
redwood routing override set --scope eu-west-1 --prefer-region true --expires 15m
```

lee: running pause now. Output: `rollout v2.3.7 paused (interactive) — traffic switched to stable v2.3.6`

priya: requested DNS provider purge for eu-edge RRSet and set temporary TTL=30s. Provider acked purge request, but propagation is still inconsistent across recursors. We'll keep monitoring.

alex: after pause we see error rate drop immediately in eu-west-1 traces. Latency trending down from +600ms to +120ms. Some residual 502s where clients still resolved to stale VIP — should clear as TTL propagates.

maria: good. Can we also add a fallback-safe check to routing logic to avoid cross-region variant fallback? Even a soft-fail that returns 429 rather than routing to incompatible variant would avoid these user-visible 5xxs.

samir: agree — filing a followup ticket to add compatibility checks in the fallback code path. For now adding a guard in the policy engine to avoid preferring other-region VIPs.

cs_ops: no new severity escalations. Top 5 affected customers contacted; two asked for request logs which we shared.

lee: handing off to maria at 14:25 UTC for next 2 hours. Notes: rollback completed, DNS purge requested, override expires in 15m (monitor), watch for oscillations when override expires. If 5xx creeps up again, reapply override and open provider escalation with DNS.

maria: taking over. Action items for next 15m: validate full propagation (dig from multiple public recursors), watch error rate on hosted API and per-tenant queues, confirm CS has all needed comms.

priya: quick diagnostic dumps:
- edge-rrset-prev: 52.11.22.33,52.11.22.34
- edge-rrset-current: 3.4.5.6,3.4.5.7
- provider-purge-id: PURGE-98123 (ack)
We still see ~20% of recursors returning old set.

alex: note: some internal canaries in ap-south still routing fine — seems limited to EU PoPs mirroring a stale zone.

maria: OK, metrics show steady improvement. Error rate down 85% in 12m. Keeping status: "degraded" until TTL fully stabilizes.

cs_ops: posting update to status page and sending an incident summary to affected account leads.

samir: follow-ups: (1) revert fallback ordering bug in the policy repo (PR in flight) (2) add pre-deploy check to validate fallback doesn't point to different region VIPs (3) DNS runbook update: reduce zone TTL for critical edge rrsets during rollouts.

maria: final note before close: require postmortem with eng-runtime + dns + routing-policy owners. Assigning owners: samir (runtime), priya (dns), maria (routing). Will schedule postmortem meeting.

lee: thanks team. I'll stay reachable if things regress. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: [INCIDENT] status: mitigated — root cause under investigation. Incident record: https://incidents.example/INC-4312
